records.material_pending_reason: The western headward pond-chain transfer into the first larger lake inlet remains unestablished. The downstream McConnell River lake-and-channel sequence and Hudson Bay outlet are mapped, but those observations do not close the initial connector.

This is one source-material-pending record, with McConnell River retained only as a bounded component/potential representative candidate, not a completed identity or naming-scope hold.

component_scope_limits: McConnell River is read on original cartography along the connected downstream corridor. It does not automatically name the initial western feeder, every lake passage, all short side streams or the selected feature as a uniform scalar.

The primary material gap is geographic connectivity at the headward transfer. A nearby river label, model line or river-system prose cannot close it.
Accepted name, whole-feature scalar name and Korean name remain null; no automatic or product application is authorized.

material_pending_components.gap: The short western pond-chain transfer into the west-side inlet of the first larger lake has not been established as continuous original-map hydrography.
material_pending_components.why_material: It joins the selected headward start to the otherwise readable McConnell corridor; without it the entire selected system cannot receive completed representative identity or completed scope hold.
material_pending_components.attempted_resolution: Independent detailed NTS065H/07 CanMatrix original requested once after successful official directory; it returned HTTP403 and is stopped.

records.region: Virginia, United States; selected inland Rappahannock region.
records.candidate_name_role: representative downstream river-system identity; not a uniform hydronym for every selected reach
records.geographic_disambiguation: Seven original USGS map views establish the full selected route from an unnamed headwater branch into North Fork Thornton, through Thornton and Hazel rivers to Rappahannock, including the Rapidan junction, Fredericksburg tidal transition and actual Leedstown–Otterburn Marsh terminal setting. Virginia DWR primary prose corroborates the downstream and tidal context. Rappahannock River is supported as representative system identity only. Accepted, scalar and Korean names remain null; application remains false.

naming_scope_details.component_scope_limits: The selected corridor combines a short unnamed headwater branch, North Fork Thornton River, Thornton River, Hazel River and Rappahannock River, ending at the Leedstown tidal bend. Rappahannock River is a representative identity only. The separate headwaters described at Chester Gap, the Rapidan upstream branch, lateral reservoirs and downstream Chesapeake Bay outlet are not the selected route. Exact hydronym-transition vertices are not assigned.

records.completion_scope: All selected FID 8857 geometry and internal multiline parts were considered at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale: initial ice opening, southeastward connector, first eastward turn, middle northward excursion, southeastward and lower eastward bends, ice/rock transitions and actual terminal sector. This is terrain correspondence, not a hydrological-continuity or exact-front survey.
records.region: Eastern Greenland; selected inner Scoresby Sund region.
records.candidate_name_role: No supported representative natural-river name; glacier, land and fjord labels are contextual only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The opening, entire ice/nunatak/rock-margin corridor and Rolige Bræ–Rødefjord terminal setting have positive overlapping original-map coverage. These observations do not establish a representative natural river, a continuous surface/subglacial river route or a hydronym for the whole selected modeled group.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected lower corridor is in the Rolige Bræ–Rødefjord sector, north of the separate Vestfjord Gletscher–Vestfjord route. The detailed original distinguishes these adjacent ice and fjord connections. Sheet 11 Kong Oscar Fjord is north of the target and contributes no selected-route evidence.

completion_scope.geographic_scale: Ordinary generalized component/corridor scale; no precise banks, surveyed spring/mouth point, current inundation or exact vertex agreement required or asserted.
completion_scope.reservoir_evidence_boundary: Original 2014 planning figure establishes Chacrillas valley reach and approaches; successful independent DOH prose establishes filling from Rocín and designed downstream water-delivery connection. This combination supports the bounded relation, while a present wetted polygon remains unclaimed.

records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-system identity for the connected selected object, not a uniform hydronym for Tambillos, Rocín, Putaendo or Chacrillas.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The full selected Tambillos–Rocín–Chacrillas–Putaendo–Aconcagua corridor and Concón estuarine/Pacific terminal are geographically supported. Río Aconcagua is a representative-system candidate only. The selected opening is distinguished from the Las Majadas side feeder; Hidalgo and Chalaco are separate tributary transitions. Chacrillas is established by original planning cartography plus independent primary infrastructure prose, without claiming a current reservoir surface.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-system identity for the connected selected object, not a uniform hydronym for Tambillos, Rocín, Putaendo or Chacrillas.

component_scope_limits: Tambillos, Rocín, Putaendo and Aconcagua are distinct local river scopes; Chacrillas is an impoundment name. None is imposed uniformly on every selected subreach.
The actual selected opening is not equated with a remote true source or named lake; Las Majadas is a separately mapped side feeder.
Broad wetland inventory labels such as Sist. Rio Aconcagua y trib do not rename all upstream branches. Missing-name values remain null.
Off-selected reservoir polygons in the Limache system are not assigned the unavailable optional Los Aromos name and are not made selected passages.
Planning cartography and historical agency prose establish ordinary reservoir connectivity, not current operation, water levels, bank positions or legal name registration.
Accepted name, whole-feature scalar name and Korean name remain null; no product or automatic application.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
